sentences: `op_sel` bits 0..2 read the high half of S0..S2, bit 3 writes the high half of D, and the unwritten half of D is kept (see *16-bit results*).

`v_min3_f16` and `v_max3_f16` read each selected f16 half through `Gen.f16_in` (`neg`/`abs` apply to the selected half), fold with `NMin`/`NMax` (so a NaN operand yields the other operand and −0 orders below +0, matching `v_min3_f32`/`v_max3_f32` and `v_med3_f16`), then apply VOP3 `omod`/`clamp` and `Gen.f16_out`.

The 16-bit integer ops zero-extend (`u16`) or sign-extend (`i16`) the selected 16-bit halves, evaluate `UMin`/`UMax`/`UClamp` or `SMin`/`SMax`/`SClamp`, and write the low 16 bits into the selected half of D; `clamp` is supported on integer min3/max3/med3 as an identity no-op on the 16-bit container (hardware-verified on gfx1036 across wave32 and wave64); non-VGPR `op_sel` destinations raise `Unsupported`.

Source: AMD [RDNA 2 ISA reference](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/radeon-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf) VOP3 opcodes `0x351`–`0x356`, `0x359`–`0x35A`, and Mesa ACO's `can_use_opsel`.

**Hardware-verified on RDNA2** (gfx1036 iGPU, AMD Windows driver 32.0.21045.16010, `tools/hw_oracle`, IEEE 0 with f16 denormals kept): 6,092 cases (every triple of ±0, a denormal, 1.0, -1.0, 2.0, ±inf, a quiet and a signalling NaN for each f16 op; every triple of 8 edge values for the i16/u16 ops; `op_sel` on each source and the destination; a 0xabcd high half on every source) give the translator's word, the kept destination half included, except one: with all three operands NaN the hardware returns src0's NaN bits unchanged (`0x7c01` stays a signalling NaN under IEEE 0), the translator a quiet NaN, as for the 32-bit ops (*Float min/max/med3 with NaN*).

`tests/semantic/test_alu_min3_max3_med3_16_hw.py` holds 540 of the measured words, and `ALL_NAN_SRC0_SIGNALLING` there holds the 8 all-NaN min3/max3 rows with a signalling src0 (an `expectedFailure` until the translator keeps src0's bits).

CPU-checked by `tests/semantic/test_alu_min3_max3_med3_16.py`, `tests/test_f16_op_sel.py`, and `tests/test_f16_op_sel_values.py`; also **hardware-verified on RDNA2** (`gfx1035`, Windows 11, driver `26.5.1`, wave32 & wave64 via `tools/int_hw_probe.py --oracle both --group valu_min3_max3_med3_16`): all eight ops (`op_sel`, untouched destination half, NaN, −0/+0 ordering, and `v_max3_f16` `clamp`) match bit-for-bit.
